messages:
nina: Heads-up: during the blue-green migration we introduced a temporary prefix alias and saw keys from the old logical namespace surface under the new prefix on the new owner. Minimal log: 

```
[2026-09-01T10:02:00Z] alias-create old_prefix=tenant9/orders new_alias=tenant9/orders_v2
[2026-09-01T10:02:01Z] handoff new_owner accepted token=ali:900
[2026-09-01T10:02:02Z] read tenant9/orders_v2:order123 -> value from old_prefix (unexpected)
```

otto: Oof. So aliasing the name without strong identity allowed the new owner to treat old-key encodings as local keys. Did the WAL records include only logical prefix string, not a stable prefix id?

sarah: Today records use the human-readable prefix and a derived namespace hash in some places, but that hash isn't authoritative and we compute it lazily at apply. That laziness is the root cause: on replay the new owner re-derived the mapping differently under alias rules.

nina: We need a stable prefix identity that travels in tokens and WAL entries. Two fixes: (1) bake a prefix_uuid into WAL headers and handoff tokens, and verify during prefill/apply; (2) tighten alias semantics so aliasing is a redirect, not a rename, until a full cutover is complete. Tradeoffs: (1) requires WAL header change and migration; (2) makes aliasing slower/more operationally heavy.

otto: I prefer (1) long-term. Quick patch for canary: reject alias-handoffs unless token includes prefix_uuid and new owner sees matching WAL header; otherwise fall back to serial prefill. That avoids the surprising contamination.

sarah: Implementation sketch for (1):
- On prefix create/rename emit stable prefix_uuid (UUIDv4) and persist to meta-store
- All subsequent WAL records include prefix_uuid in header (8-16B)
- Demote/handback tokens include prefix_uuid signed by old owner
- New owner verifies token.prefix_uuid == record.header.prefix_uuid when applying; mismatch -> treat as conflict and request explicit delta prefill

nina: Also add a runtime invariant check (debug-only) that samples applied records post-handback and asserts header prefix_uuid == active_prefix_uuid. Will catch edgecases early in canary.

otto: Small ops concern: adding prefix_uuid to WAL increases record size slightly and requires rolling upgrade. We can encode prefix_uuid compactly (8 byte) and allow older nodes to emit legacy zeros; new owner treats zero as "untrusted" and forces full prefill for that prefix. That gives safe incremental rollout.

sarah: Need telemetry: alias-handback-conflicts, legacy-wal-prefill-rate, prefix-uuid-mismatch-alerts. Gate via FF so we can enable on a few clusters first.

ci-bot: Created ticket RM-11221: "prefix-uuid-and-alias-safety" assigned to otto + sarah. :white_check_mark:

nina: Thanks team. I'll add a short note in the migration playbook: avoid creating ephemeral aliases without prefix_uuid support enabled. @oncall FYI. :pray:
